parameters.excerpt: The hardware platform may define that accesses to certain CSRs are strongly ordered, as defined by the Memory-Ordering PMAs section in Volume II of this manual.
parameters.modal_signal: may define that accesses to certain CSRs are strongly ordered
parameters.reasoning: The hardware platform may define certain CSRs as strongly ordered — this is a platform-level memory ordering choice. While it contains optionality language ('may define'), it is a platform/PMA-level decision rather than a pure ISA architectural parameter, making it NON_ISA. However, it is borderline since it affects ISA-visible behavior. Classified NON_ISA because it references the Memory-Ordering PMAs section (a platform-level concept) and is a platform-level choice.

skipped_non_parameters.excerpt: If _rd_=`x0`, then the instruction shall not read the CSR and shall not cause any of the side effects that might occur on a CSR read.
skipped_non_parameters.reason: Fixed requirement ('shall not') binding on all implementations — no implementer choice here.

skipped_non_parameters.excerpt: For both CSRRS and CSRRC, if _rs1_=`x0`, then the instruction will not write to the CSR at all, and so shall not cause any of the side effects that might otherwise occur on a CSR write, nor raise illegal-instruction exceptions on accesses to read-only CSRs.
skipped_non_parameters.reason: Fixed behavioral requirement ('shall not') describing mandatory ISA behavior, not an implementation choice.

skipped_non_parameters.excerpt: Some CSRs, such as the instructions-retired counter, `instret`, may be modified as side effects of instruction execution.
skipped_non_parameters.reason: 'May be modified' here is a statement of fact about possible side effects, not an implementer optionality signal. This describes ISA-defined behavior, not a parameter.

skipped_non_parameters.excerpt: For the RVWMO memory consistency model (<<memorymodel>>), CSR accesses are weakly ordered by default, so other harts or devices may observe CSR accesses in an order different from program order.
skipped_non_parameters.reason: This is a fixed behavioral rule of the RVWMO memory model, not an implementation choice. 'May observe' is a permission statement about observers, not an implementer optionality signal.

skipped_non_parameters.excerpt: Unless specified otherwise, the full consequences of any such side effects are observable by the very next instruction, and no consequences may be observed out-of-order by preceding instructions.
skipped_non_parameters.reason: Fixed requirement about synchronous side-effect ordering ('no consequences may be observed out-of-order'). This is a mandatory rule, not an implementer choice.
